Geoffrey Drumm joins Danny Jones to present what the title calls new proof of the Great Pyramid's true purpose. Drumm argues the great stone work was no tomb. He says it was a machine built for a lost use.

Drumm walks through the shafts, chambers, and stone choices that he says point to a working plant. He ties the design to power and to chemical work in the deep rooms. Jones asks how the claim can be tested. Listeners who love pyramid lore get a fresh form of the case. The library holds the episode as an archive record, without a verdict on the claim.

A survivor of the USS Liberty attack joins Tucker Carlson to tell what he says truly happened the day Israel hit the ship. The title also names the lies he says still cover it up. The attack took place in 1967 and killed 34 US sailors.

The survivor tells the attack as he lived it, hour by hour, from the deck of the ship. He argues the strike was no error and that US leaders helped bury the truth. Carlson asks why the case stays shut after so long. Listeners hear a grave first hand tale. The library keeps the talk as a record of his account.
uslaw-usc-t2-s167i: Section 167i of Title 2 of the United States Code lets the Librarian of Congress loosen the bans on using Library buildings and grounds for approved ceremonies. It sits in the chapter on the Library of Congress. For such a ceremony, the Librarian may pause as much of the bans in sections 5103 and 5104 of Title 40 as the event needs. The pause requires named officers in charge. It also requires plans the Librarian judges fit to keep order and protect the buildings, grounds, people, and property.
